en: The Archimedes screw uses the inclined plane and screw simple machines to lift water for irrigation in ancient Greece.
Teflon, a synthetic fluoropolymer invented by Roy Plunkett, has an extremely low coefficient of friction, making it ideal for non-stick pans.
Astronauts on the Moon can jump six times higher than on Earth because the Moon's gravitational pull is much weaker.
Ancient Chinese navigators used pieces of naturally magnetized lodestone to create the first magnetic compasses for directional ocean navigation.
Alessandro Volta invented the voltaic pile in 1800, which was the first true electrical battery capable of producing steady current.
The Aurora Borealis occurs when charged solar particles collide with gases in Earth's upper atmosphere to emit colorful visible light.
Sperm whales communicate underwater by producing clicks up to 230 decibels, making them the loudest sound-producing animals on Earth.
Old Faithful, a famous geyser in Yellowstone National Park, erupts when underground groundwater is heated by magma until it boils.
The Three Gorges Dam in China converts the kinetic energy of the flowing Yangtze River into electrical energy using turbines.
Seatbelts protect passengers during a sudden car crash by providing an unbalanced force to counteract the passengers' forward inertia.
Photovoltaic solar panels transform radiant light energy from the Sun directly into usable electrical energy to power homes.
George de Mestral invented Velcro after observing how tiny hooks on plant burrs increased friction to stick to animal fur.
